title: Majestic Sacrifices: The Pawn Ending
summary: After the heavy pieces disappear, improve the king before committing the spare pawns. The wrong pawn push changes the exact result.

nodes.question: Should Black activate the king or push a pawn?
nodes.explanation: Begin in the separate pawn ending at 65s, with Black to move after White’s king has reached g5. Black has Kd4 and pawns f5/g7/h7 against Kg5 and pawns g3/h4.

branches.title: Independent king activation and pawn conversion
commentary: Begin in the separate pawn ending at 65s, with Black to move after White’s king has reached g5. Black has Kd4 and pawns f5/g7/h7 against Kg5 and pawns g3/h4.
Ke4 activates the king and preserves Black’s exact win. It threatens to approach the white pawns from f3.
h5 runs White’s outside pawn in this independent representative defense.
Kf3 heads toward g3 while Black still has g7 available to stop the h-pawn.
h6 moves within two steps of promotion.
gxh6+ removes the passer with check against Kg5.
Kxh6 recaptures, but the white king has been diverted from g3.
Kxg3 removes White’s remaining pawn. Black keeps the f5 passer and h7 pawn.
Kg5 returns toward the central passer. This is a representative legal continuation, not a claim of best defense at every turn.
f4 starts the promotion march while Black’s king supports its route.
Kf5 approaches the f-pawn but cannot capture it while Kg3 controls f4.
f3 advances the protected passer.
Ke4 takes a different route toward the pawn.
f2 leaves only one step to promotion.
Kd3 cannot reach f1 in time in this selected continuation.
f1=Q+ promotes with check. The exact queen-and-pawn versus king ending is winning for Black.

exercises.prompt: Why keep the pawn moves in reserve?
exercises.answer: King activation puts pressure on the white pawns while retaining g7 as a response to h5–h6. The exact comparisons show that g6 draws and h6+ even loses for Black.

startContext: Begin only in the seven-piece pawn ending shown at 65s with White Kg5 and Black Kd4. The earlier knight/bishop sacrifices, larger rook-check sequence and later pawn mate remain source context. All encoded continuations from this saved ending are independent representative lines; Black is the practice side and must preserve a win.
verification_scope: Saved board images reviewed manually. Every encoded intermediate position and endpoint is checked against the tablebase. Selected instructive variations, not an exhaustive tree of all legal defenses.
